card.name: Linking words before patient-condition restrictions
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (a comma, 'or', 'after', 'a', 'should') right after a medical condition or procedure, just before a restriction or caution. Also 'Tablets' after a drug name before 'in patients with...'.

modes.label: Link after condition
modes.description: A comma, 'or' or 'after' directly after a condition, surgery or event, leading into a caution or contraindication.
modes.example: Breast cancer<< or>> a history of breast cancer (4,

modes.label: Tablets after drug name
modes.description: The word 'Tablets' after a drug name, introducing a patient group in a caution.
modes.example: Avoid the use of Pentazocine and Naloxone<< Tablets>> in patients with impaired consciousness or coma.

card.writes: Little clear effect, though it suppresses travel words, so it mainly keeps the text in drug-label caution language.
card.plain: It fires on small joining words in a warning sentence, just before the text says what to avoid or watch for in certain patients.
